_headline: THE REGULATION WILL NOT NAME THE STANDARD; THE REPORT PUBLISHED UNDER THE REGULATION NAMES IT OUTRIGHT. Implementing Regulation (EU) 2016/2304 recital (5) refers only to 'the European Statistical System standards on quality reporting published by the Commission (Eurostat)' — AGENCY ONLY, and a search of all 24,942 characters for SIMS, ESMS, ESQRS or Handbook returns nothing. The Eurostat report produced under that same Regulation says the assessment adheres 'to the requirements for the Single Integrated Metadata Structure'. Same standard; only the non-legislative document will say its name. That is G.50.md's two-layer finding — legislative layer names nobody, self-regulatory layer names its sources freely — reproduced inside ONE chain, with the boundary falling exactly between an instrument and the report published under it.
_second_finding: THE TWO INSTRUMENTS ARE COMPLEMENTARY FAILURES, AND THAT IS WHY NO MEMBER-STATE NODE EXISTS IN EITHER SLICE. Regulation 479/2009 Article 9(4) compels a PUBLISHED national document ('Member States shall make their inventories public') but states no interval, only an event trigger. Implementing Regulation 2016/2304 states the interval ('Member States shall provide the quality report on an annual basis') and compels NO publication — searched for 'shall be made public', 'publish', 'publication', 'public' across the whole instrument; the two hits are Eurostat's own standards and the Regulation's entry into force. Each instrument supplies exactly what the other lacks and neither supplies both. Two slices, two compelled national document classes, 54 documents in principle, and zero mintable member-state nodes — for two different and individually sufficient reasons.
_third_finding: THE EU COMPELS THE NAMING IT WILL NOT DO ITSELF. Annex 4.2 indicator 2 of 2016/2304 requires each Member State to supply a 'List of national publications on the data sources used and methodology applied containing the titles of these publications and links to them, if available' — annually, all 27. Every EU instrument this branch has followed has stopped at AGENCY ONLY at the national boundary, and this one does too on its own face. But it REQUIRES the member states to name their own publications by title. Read against EU/slices/README.md's disclosure-runs-upward finding, this is a candidate mechanism for that asymmetry: the upward disclosure may not be voluntary candour at the national end but a reporting requirement drafted at the supranational end. Offered as an observation, not a conclusion — establishing it would need a national quality report, and none is published.
_open_questions: THE CHEAPEST HIGH-VALUE TEST IN THE EU BRANCH IS NOW SPECIFIC: does any Member State publish its own ESA 2010 quality report voluntarily? Nothing compels it (see _second_finding), but nothing forbids it either, and one such document would be a list of national statistical publications by title with links — the 'document that names its own inputs in a table' that Research.1.md §7 calls the strongest evidence class there is, for one country, annually. If even one exists, the member-state layer opens by a route neither Annex B nor Annex XI nor Article 9 of 479/2009 could open. If none exists, that is a measured negative across 27 jurisdictions and worth as much.

eurostat-national-accounts-quality-report is minted at releases_per_year 1 on the publication's own count — 'It is the eighth such report since the European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010) was introduced in September 2014' — corroborated by eight observed editions across 2018-2025 and by an ISSN. Note the editions are not a clean annual series by reference year: the 2018 edition covers 2016 data and the 2019 edition covers 2018 data, so no edition covers 2017 data. The PUBLICATION cadence is annual; the COVERAGE has a gap. Flagged rather than smoothed.

Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2016/2304 is deliberately NOT minted as a node. EUR-Lex shows no consolidated versions of it, so on the observed-record basis used for eu-reg-479-2009 and eu-reg-223-2009 it has been published once — and Research.1.md §4.2 is explicit that 'something published once is not a node'. It appears in three basis fields instead. If a future session finds it amended, revisit.

esa-2010's releases_per_year of 0.05 gets a second datum against it. EUR-Lex lists FOUR consolidated versions of Regulation 549/2013 — 16/07/2013, 24/08/2015, 01/09/2024, 01/09/2025 — which is roughly 0.33 a year, not 0.05. esa-2010.json's own _open_questions already flags the 0.05 as matched to sna-2008 by precedent rather than by arithmetic. This is a second reason to look, not a new answer, and changing it is not this slice's call. Note also that Article 4 was read in the 24/08/2015 text, not the current 01/09/2025 one.

reports.title: Quality report on national and regional accounts
reports.description: Eurostat's annual assessment of the quality of the national and regional accounts data that Member States transmit under the ESA 2010 transmission programme, produced under Article 4 of Regulation (EU) No 549/2013 and structured by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2016/2304. In its own words: 'This document presents Eurostat's assessment of the quality of national and regional accounts data submitted by the EU Member States, as well as Iceland, Norway and Switzerland, in 2024. It also includes information on the quality of key European aggregates published by Eurostat. The assessment in this quality report is based on the national quality reports exercise for data transmissions during 2024.' Distinct from eurostat-edp-gfs-quality-report, which is the Article 8(3) report on fiscal data under Regulation 479/2009 — the two are adjacent and easily conflated. This node is the one document in the chain that names the Single Integrated Metadata Structure by name; the Regulation governing it does not.
reports.cadence_note: Stated by the publication itself — 'It is the eighth such report since the European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010) was introduced in September 2014' — and corroborated by eight observed editions across 2018-2025 (KS-FT-18-004, KS-FT-19-009, KS-FT-20-007, KS-FT-21-009, KS-FT-22-008, KS-FT-23-002, KS-01-24-023, KS-01-25-052) and by ISSN 2529-3222. The underlying obligation is annual on its face: 'Member States shall provide the quality report on an annual basis' (Implementing Regulation 2016/2304, Article 1). See _open_questions on the reference-year gap.

reports.title: Regulation (EC) No 223/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council on European statistics
reports.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
reports.description: The framework Regulation for European statistics, and the legal spine EU/slices/README.md names alongside ESA 2010 and the EBS Regulation. Two of its articles do work across this corpus. Article 11 constitutes the European Statistics Code of Practice: 'The Code of Practice shall aim at ensuring public trust in European statistics by establishing how European statistics are to be developed, produced and disseminated in conformity with the statistical principles as set out in Article 2(1) and best international statistical practice', and 'The Code of Practice shall be reviewed and updated as necessary by the ESS Committee. The Commission shall publish amendments thereto.' Article 12(1) sets the seven quality criteria — relevance, accuracy, timeliness, punctuality, accessibility and clarity, comparability, coherence — that ESA 2010 Article 4(1) applies to transmitted data and that Implementing Regulation 2016/2304 structures the national quality reports around. Minted 2026-08-07 after G.50.md filed it deferred when EUR-Lex served nothing; the retry G.50 recommended succeeded.
reports.cadence_note: Derived from an observed amendment record, not a stated rate, on the same basis as eu-reg-479-2009 in the sibling slice. Adopted 11 March 2009; EUR-Lex lists two consolidated versions, 08/06/2015 and 26/12/2024, with 26/12/2024 flagged as current. Two amendments across the 17 years to 2026.

release_schedule.note: Regulation (EC) No 223/2009 is a standing legal act (the framework regulation governing the European Statistical System), not a periodically released publication. It has been amended irregularly as legislative need arose — e.g. by Regulation (EU) 2015/759, Regulation (EU) 2019/2152 (ESS governance regulation), and most recently Regulation (EU) 2024/... (in force from 26 Dec 2024, reflected in the consolidated text CELEX:02009R0223-20241226). No article of the regulation sets a fixed periodic review/evaluation date, and no publisher calendar exists for future amendments — the timing of the next amendment (if any) depends on future Commission legislative proposals and cannot be computed.

reports.title: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2016/2304 of 19 December 2016 on the modalities, structure, periodicity and assessment indicators of the quality reports on data transmitted pursuant to Regulation (EU) No 549/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council
reports.description: The Implementing Regulation that structures the annual national-accounts quality reports Member States submit under ESA 2010 (Regulation 549/2013) — the same instrument eurostat-national-accounts-quality-report's own description already names as what it is 'structured by'. Article 1 sets the periodicity for the underlying obligation, not for itself: 'Member States shall provide the quality report on an annual basis' with reports due no later than 31 May each year. Minted 2026-08-08 as a one-off foundational instrument under Research.1.md §4 (Thomas's ruling): adopted once (19 December 2016) and never amended — EUR-Lex shows no consolidated version — which is exactly the shape the new rule was written to admit; previously excluded under the old §4.2 language ('something published once is not a node'), recorded in this file's _dropped array until today. No predecessor is named anywhere in the instrument or in G.50/G.52's research, so it is not read as a recast — a genuine one-off, not a lineage's current edition.

dependencies.basis: Quality report on national and regional accounts, 2025 edition (KS-01-25-052), Executive summary, page 5: 'The quality assessment was carried out in accordance with Article 4 of the ESA 2010 Regulation (Regulation (EU) No 549/2013).' The dependence is on the instrument for the method and on its Annex B for the scope of what is assessed — Implementing Regulation (EU) 2016/2304 Article 1: 'The quality report on national and regional accounts referred to in Article 4(2) of Regulation (EU) No 549/2013 shall cover the data sent by Member States in accordance with the ESA 2010 transmission programme as laid down in Annex B to Regulation (EU) No 549/2013 in the year preceding the report.' 'In accordance with' is derivation language and is not on Research.1.md §5a's watchlist. Direction: the report is the dependent. Read from the source PDF 2026-08-07.

Quality report on national and regional accounts, 2025 edition (KS-01-25-052), Executive summary, page 5: 'The quality report covers a number of quality indicators (completeness, revision policy and practice, punctuality, coherence and documentation on methodology), adhering to the requirements for the Single Integrated Metadata Structure, which were endorsed by the European Statistical System Committee in November 2015.' 'Adhering to the requirements for' is obligation language, not §5a agreement language. THIS EDGE IS THE SLICE'S HEADLINE: the Implementing Regulation that governs this report declines to name SIMS, calling it only 'the European Statistical System standards on quality reporting published by the Commission (Eurostat)' (recital 5), and a search of the whole instrument for 'SIMS', 'Single Integrated', 'ESMS', 'ESQRS' and 'Handbook' returns zero hits. The report names it. Read from the source PDF 2026-08-07.

Quality report on national and regional accounts, 2025 edition (KS-01-25-052), Executive summary, page 5: 'This requires the quality of national and regional accounts data sent to Eurostat to be assessed against the quality criteria set out in the Regulation on European statistics (Regulation (EC) No 223/2009).' The criteria themselves are Article 12(1): 'To guarantee the quality of results, European statistics shall be developed, produced and disseminated on the basis of uniform standards and of harmonised methods. In this respect, the following quality criteria shall apply: (a) relevance … (g) coherence', and Implementing Regulation 2016/2304's Annex §3 structures the reports around them: 'The quality reports shall include information on all the quality criteria laid down in Article 12(1) of Regulation (EC) No 223/2009. The information shall be presented according to the following structure: Relevance; Accuracy and reliability; Timeliness and punctuality; Accessibility and clarity; Coherence and comparability.' Both documents read from source 2026-08-07.

Regulation (EU) No 549/2013, consolidated text of 24/08/2015, Article 4(1) ('Quality assessment'): 'For the purpose of this Regulation, the quality criteria set out in Article 12(1) of Regulation (EC) No 223/2009 shall apply to the data to be transmitted in accordance with Article 3 of this Regulation.' 'Shall apply' is application of one instrument's criteria by another, not comparability — §5a does not reach it. Direction: ESA 2010 is the dependent, taking its quality criteria from the framework Regulation. NOTE THAT THIS IS esa-2010'S FIRST OUTGOING DEPENDENCY IN THE CORPUS: it was imported with zero, and its only previously proposed outgoing edge (esa-2010 -> sna-2008) is refused by §5a in esa-2010.json and refused again by a fourth independent statement found this session (see _dropped). Read from EUR-Lex 2026-08-07.

eurostat-national-accounts-quality-report's own description: 'produced under Article 4 of Regulation (EU) No 549/2013 and structured by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2016/2304.' The Regulation sets the modalities, structure, periodicity and assessment indicators the report follows — method, not raw data input, hence methodology_depends_on rather than uses_data_from. Added 2026-08-08 alongside minting the target node; the edge was implicit in the source node's description since the file was drafted but could not be minted while the target had no node.

_dropped.why: G.50.md's DEFERRED ITEM, NOW SETTLED — AND NOT THE WAY IT EXPECTED. G.50 filed this edge deferred purely on retrieval: EUR-Lex served nothing, and the staged Article 11(1)/(2) quotes 'would support both a Regulation node and this edge'. The retry G.50 recommended succeeded, both articles are verified verbatim, and the Regulation node is minted above. THE EDGE IS STILL NOT MINTED, for a reason invisible from the Regulation's side. The Code of Practice's own preamble says: 'The common quality framework of the European Statistical System is composed of the European Statistics Code of Practice, the Quality Assurance Framework of the European Statistical System and the general quality management principles … This self-regulatory common quality framework COMPLEMENTS the extensive legal framework of the European Statistical System based on the Regulation (EC) No 223/2009 on European statistics which itself derives from the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union.' 'Complements' is §5a family, and it is not loose phrasing — the sentence exists to draw a line between a 'self-regulatory' framework and a 'legal framework' and to put the Code of Practice on the self-regulatory side. Against that, Regulation 223/2009 Article 11 asserts authority over the Code: 'The Code of Practice shall aim at ensuring public trust in European statistics by establishing how European statistics are to be developed, produced and disseminated in conformity with the statistical principles as set out in Article 2(1)' and 'The Code of Practice shall be reviewed and updated as necessary by the ESS Committee.' TWO DOCUMENTS POINTING OPPOSITE WAYS, BOTH QUOTED, NEITHER PICKED, per Research.1.md §3. Reason moved from 'deferred' (a retrieval problem, solved) to a documented conflict. NOT FOUND: no other citation of Regulation 223/2009 anywhere in the CoP's 11 pages, and no occurrence of 'Article 11' (strings searched: '223/2009', 'Regulation (EC) No 223/2009', 'Article 11').

DOCUMENTED PLAINLY AND BLOCKED ON PUBLICATION, WHICH IS THE SLICE'S SECOND FINDING. The report says what it is built from: 'The assessment in this quality report is based on the national quality reports exercise for data transmissions during 2024.' The Implementing Regulation compels those reports annually from all 27 — 'Every year, not later than 31 May, Member States shall provide the Commission (Eurostat) with the completed quality report' — and NOTHING IN THE INSTRUMENT REQUIRES THEM TO BE PUBLISHED. Strings searched across all 24,942 characters of 2016/2304: 'shall be made public', 'publish', 'publication', 'public'. The only two hits are recital 5 (standards published by Eurostat) and Article 3 (the Regulation's own entry into force on publication in the Official Journal). Compare Regulation 479/2009 Article 9(4), 'Member States shall make their inventories public', which is what made the EDP inventories a published class in the sibling slice. Research.1.md §4 requires a node to be published on a cadence; these are produced on a cadence and not published. AGENCY ONLY as to which reports, additionally: neither the Regulation nor the Eurostat report names a single Member State's quality report.

THE TEMPTING EDGE, AND IT FAILS TWICE OVER. Recital (5): 'As the information in the quality reports on national and regional accounts should be based on the European Statistical System standards on quality reporting published by the Commission (Eurostat), the Annex to this Regulation should be drawn up in line with those standards.' The standard meant is SIMS — the report published under this very Regulation says so (see the minted edge above), and Eurostat's own quality-reporting page says 'The ESS quality reporting standard is the Single Integrated Metadata Structure (SIMS)', which is what G.50.md minted ess-sims on. But the Regulation will not say it. Searched the full instrument: 'SIMS' NOT FOUND, 'Single Integrated' NOT FOUND, 'ESMS' NOT FOUND, 'ESQRS' NOT FOUND, 'handbook'/'Handbook' NOT FOUND. That is AGENCY ONLY in Research.1.md §6's sense, applied to a standard rather than to a publisher. Second and independent reason: 'should be drawn up in line with' is recital language and 'in line with' is §5a family. Recorded in full because this is exactly the edge a future session will re-propose from the recital alone.

_dropped.edge: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2016/2304 as a node
_dropped.why: RESOLVED 2026-08-08 — Research.1.md §4's rule change (Thomas's ruling) admits one-off foundational instruments (treaty, trade deal, government policy/regulation, adopted once) as nodes without a cadence. This entry's original blocker was the old §4.2 language, 'something published once is not a node' — that is the exact clause the ruling replaced. Re-checked against EUR-Lex this session: still no consolidated/amended version, still a genuine one-off, not a recast (no predecessor named anywhere). Minted as eu-reg-2016-2304, releases_per_year absent (evergreen, not guessed), with a methodology_depends_on edge from eurostat-national-accounts-quality-report added in the same pass. Original note preserved below for the research trail. ORIGINAL: DELIBERATELY NOT MINTED, and the reasoning should be reusable. EUR-Lex shows no consolidated versions of 2016/2304 — on the observed-record basis used for eu-reg-479-2009 and eu-reg-223-2009 it has been published once and never amended, and Research.1.md §4.2 is explicit that 'something published once is not a node'. It appears in three basis fields instead, which is where an instrument that determines a method but does not recur belongs. This is the same call, made the same way, as the corpus's treatment of one-off implementing decisions. Revisit if a future session finds it amended.

A FOURTH INDEPENDENT §5a STATEMENT ON AN EDGE ALREADY REFUSED THREE TIMES, recorded because esa-2010.json predicts it will keep being re-proposed and notes it already was once. Quality report on national and regional accounts, 2025 edition, §3.3 'Manuals and guidelines': 'ESA 2010 is broadly aligned with SNA 2008 to make comparable analysis with non-EU economies possible.' Two watchlist phrases in fourteen words — 'broadly aligned with' and 'comparable analysis'. The three already recorded in esa-2010.json are 'is consistent with' (ESA 2010 Annex A ¶1.05), 'is fully consistent with' (the supply-and-use manual) and 'fully consistent with' (Eurostat's national accounts page). Four statements, four different documents, all agreement language, none a dependency.

_dropped.edge: esa-2010 -> NACE, CPA, COICOP, COFOG, NUTS
_dropped.why: THE STRONGEST STATEMENT YET FOR THE BRANCH'S BIGGEST CLASSIFICATION GAP, and not mintable here. Quality report on national and regional accounts, 2025 edition, §3.2, headed 'Classifications used in ESA 2010': 'Classification of institutional sectors • Statistical Classification of Economic Activities in the European Community (NACE), Rev. 2 (2008) • Statistical Classification of Products by Activity, Version 2.1 (CPA) • Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose (COICOP), COICOP 2018 • Classifications of functions of government (COFOG) • Nomenclature of territorial units for statistics (NUTS), 2024 version'. 'Used in' is a use claim, from Eurostat, about a node this corpus already holds — and not one of the five is a node, while naics, isic and anzsic all are. NOT MINTED for two reasons. First, the targets do not exist. Second, Research.1.md §7's counter-intuitive rule says a classification hub should be built from the programmes coded to it, not from a list that names it — 'Do not research a classification standard by reading the classification.' A bulleted list under a heading also gives no citable location per classification, which is why this is one record naming five things rather than five records. Logged in planning/rolling-todo.md as a candidate category.

Recorded because both ends are now nodes and the citation is real, so the edge will look available. Regulation 479/2009 Article 8(2): 'Member States shall provide the Commission (Eurostat), as promptly as possible, with the relevant statistical information requested for the needs of the data quality assessment, WITHOUT PREJUDICE TO the provisions of Regulation (EC) No 223/2009 … relating to statistical confidentiality.' A savings clause is not a dependency — it disclaims interference with another instrument rather than taking anything from it. Contrast the minted esa-2010 -> eu-reg-223-2009 edge, where Article 4(1) says the criteria 'shall apply'.

_dropped.edge: The Annex 4.2 lists of national publications
_dropped.why:
PARTIALLY ADVANCED 2026-08-09 (sweep session, Tier-3 item), still not minted. A real candidate was found: Germany's own Statistisches Bundesamt (Destatis) publishes a 'Quality Report - National Accounts' (destatis.de/EN/Methods/Quality/QualityReports/National-Accounts-Domestic-Product/) — exactly the voluntary national quality report this entry hoped might exist. But the cadence test this project requires was not cleared: the page states only a single publication date ('Date: 29 October 2025') with no reference-period or 'annual' language, and the only hint of recurrence is the PDF's own URL carrying a version parameter (`v=11`) and an external search result surfacing the same document under the label 'National Accounts - 10/2024 - 09/2025' — suggestive of a revision history and a rolling reference window, but not a stated cadence in the document's own text. Destatis's quality-reports landing page adds only that 'Since 2005, the Federal Statistical Office has offered Quality Reports on all federal statistics' — a standing practice, not a per-report frequency statement. Not minted on this evidence; the next step is opening the PDF's own text (not just its metadata) for a stated update frequency, or checking whether v=1 through v=10 are still resolvable as dated prior editions. Original entry follows.

NOT AN EDGE — A LEAD, AND THE BEST ONE EITHER SLICE PRODUCED. Implementing Regulation 2016/2304, Annex 4.2, qualitative indicator 2 ('Documentation on methodology') requires each Member State to supply: 'List of national publications on the data sources used and methodology applied containing the titles of these publications and links to them, if available'. Indicators 1 and 3 similarly require 'links to existing metadata published nationally'. So the EU compels, annually and from all 27, precisely the naming that every EU instrument this branch has read declines to do itself. If any Member State publishes its own quality report voluntarily — nothing requires it, nothing forbids it — that single document is a data-sources table in Research.1.md §7's strongest-evidence-class sense, for one country, refreshed every year. Finding one is now the cheapest high-value test in the EU branch. Note the limit of what this licenses: it makes the upward-disclosure asymmetry look like a drafting artefact rather than national candour, but establishing that needs a report in hand, and none has been read.
